newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-AGNELLI MISSES MEMORABLE DATE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-AGNELLI MISSES MEMORABLE DATE.

text.p: Juventus owner Giovanni Agnelli turned down a date with the "Old Lady" of Italian soccer on Sunday for dinner with Cuba's Fidel Castro -- and missed one of the best matches of the serie A season.

Despite the 0-0 scoreline and rain-drenched night, the clash between "La Vecchia Signora" (The Old Lady) -- the popular nickname given to Juve -- and their historic rivals Milan more than lived up to expectations.
"Thank you Champions," wrote sport's daily Gazzetta dello Sport on Monday, "0-0 but with a thousand thrills."

In a fascinating contrast in styles, European champions Juventus relied on pressure and possession while reigning Italian champions Milan preferred "il catenaccio" (the bolt) -- defending in numbers and catching Juve on the counter-attack.

Only the reflexes of goalkeepers Angelo Peruzzi and Sebastiano Rossi, a commanding performance from Franco Baresi in Milan's defence and the upright that Michele Padovano hit in the 60th minute denied 55,000 spectators at the "Delle Alpi" a goal.
However, neither Milan nor Juventus have won a league match in a month and now find themselves rubbing shoulders with the likes of Vicenza and Bologna in the serie A standings.
Juventus lie equal third with Bologna on 16 points, one behind Vicenza and two adrift of leaders Inter; Milan are in level sixth-place with Roma and Sampdoria on 14.
"The oldest match in our history was filled with regret," wrote Gazzetta dello Sport in a front-page editorial, "Juve has lost consistency, Milan lacks points."

Three wins in their last nine matches is hardly the ideal send-off for Juventus on the eve of a tough Champions League match at Manchester United followed by the Intercontinental Cup final in Tokyo with Argentina's River Plate.
A glance at the Turin side's goals for reveals the heart of the problem -- just 11 in nine matches.
With the likes of France's Didier Deschamps and Zinedine Zidane and Italy's Angelo Di Livio in midfield, this Juventus team will always enjoy a lion's share of possession.

But despite Alen Boksic's ability to scythe through defences, the side lacks a natural goalscorer -- although questions remain over coach Marcello Lippi's decision to keep Alessandro Del Piero on the bench until the 86th minute.
Milan may lie further down the table but, unlike their great rivals, they have the chance to reduce Inter's lead when they meet the leaders in the Milan derby next weekend.
The champions approach that match in confident mood following the recovery of form of Roberto Baggio and the return to fitness of their captain Franco Baresi.
Baggio failed to score on Sunday night, but his all-round performance against his old team, including a rare willingness to fight for the ball, suggested his talent still shines.
The former Italy international was only denied a goal in the 62nd minute when his delicate chip over Peruzzi was unwittingly deflected over the bar by a fortunate Juventus defender.
It was not by chance that the presence of "Kaiser Franz" Baresi in the heart of Milan's defence coincided with Paolo Maldini's and goalkeeper Rossi's best performances of the season.
"He's our leader," Croat Zvonimir Boban told Reuters after the match, "he dictates the rhythm of the side."
Despite his 36-years, Baresi seemed to be everywhere in the Milan penalty area; with his return, Milan's main problem is whether or not their captain retires at the end of the season.
"There was a defeat behind last night's return to form," wrote La Repubblica newspaper, "Milan seems incapable of building a future without Baresi."
